summary: Nora is no longer handed a block of her own records that nothing tells her how to read.
details: The top of her prompt carries a short list of what she is being shown — the room's messages, what she remembers about the person talking, the group's open questions, and so on. One block was missing from that list: the record of what her own background loop already did across the group. She was being given it every turn with no line saying what it was, which invites a model to decide for itself.

The block itself was correct and carried its own framing, so nothing unsafe reached her; what was missing was the introduction. It now has one, and the list is checked against what is actually rendered rather than kept in step by hand — so the next block cannot arrive unannounced.
limitations: The list is still written by a person, only now it cannot silently disagree with what she is served. Deriving it from one declaration per block is the larger refactor tracked separately.
